claims.claim: Reviewers note that the single-player campaign is relatively short, with completion times falling around five to ten hours.

citations.review_text:
World-class traversal and shooting, great and fun campaign...but short.

Titanfall makes you wish it had a longer campaign with more set pieces.

I ended up waiting until this game was on sale becuase I've been eyeing it for a long time. I'm honestly disappointed in the story length but I don't fault it too hard due to modern gaming shifting entirely into MMO and battle royale styled games. The story is good and there is some very fun movement mechanics. I enjoyed my time playing it, but I finished the main storyline with most of the collectables on "hard" in sub 8hrs. Worth the 50% off

That was probably the first time when I didn't expect the game to end so quickly. 
The only thing that I can say about the campaign - it was short, but great. It took only about 5 hours to complete it. 
There's something special about this product and its setting and history - something that Apex Legends lacks the most.
It's sad to see what the series has turned into with all these inclusive characters with no story and development, a ton of skins and vibrant visuals.
[b] In conclusion, I would strongly recommend giving it a go [/b]

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight movement mechanics like wall-running and sliding as smooth and central to the gameplay.

citations.review_text:
This game is awesome, I only played the campaign but it has very compelling protagonists (the titan is more of a protagonist than the player character) the dialogue although millenial-adjacent is surprisingly entertaining.

The main schtick of the game as a pilot is movement and it nails it, you run like sonic and the wallbouncing is super fluid and responsive, same with the slides, the shooting feel great too. As a titan the main schtick is all the defense/offense buttons and I can tell you its like playing a piano, awesome experience once you get the hang of it.

The story is good but the lore is whatever, you are a rebel against an evil organization or something but the way it is told makes it very engagin, overall 9/10, it runs super smoothly too.

[b]Titanfall 2[/b] is a near-perfect action FPS, whether as a single-player or a multiplayer title.

The single-player campaign is a short but intense ride through a mech-filled futuristic war. Take control of a Titan, form a bond with it, and fight against the Interstellar Manufacturing Corporation! The story cleverly incorporates gameplay mechanics like wall-running, time travel, and auto-aim, resulting in an excellent, action-packed thriller. In a world full of franchises and endless sequels, this game truly stands out. You don’t need to have played the first game, as this one stands perfectly well on its own.

The vertical gameplay is incredibly smooth, making the multiplayer experience especially unique.

Don’t sleep on this game - it’s often on sale and dirt cheap!

[u]8,5/10[/u]

I played tf1 (300hrs) and tf2 (1100hrs) on xbox and being able to play on pc was an exciting thing for me as a fan....... not in australia. 

Its extremley sad that this game is nearly dead in aus. If you want to play you have to play within peak times during the evening and its still difficult to find a full game or play on servers from across the world. 

This game is the best shooter that the medium has to offer in everyway. CoD never would have gone the way it did with its movement without TF1, it was a game full of flaws and questionable game desigin but revolutionary none the less. TF2 is the perfect sequel that did not get the attention it deserved because EA decided to sandwich its release between the 2 BIGGEST GAMES OF THAT YEAR being battlefield and CoD. 

10/10 Movement
10/10 Gunplay
10/10 Story
10/10 Artstyle
10/10 Customisation
10/10 Freedom of Expression

Please help revive this game and see how good it is for yourself, it goes on sale for $5 AUD nearly every sale.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players enjoy the campaign despite its short runtime, though they report that matchmaking takes time due to limited player counts.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign is relatively short.

citations.review_text:
My expectations for Titanfall 2 were very high, and I am happy to say that this game didn't disappoint me in the slightest.

In terms of gameplay, Titanfall is a first person shooter where you can either play as the Pilot or as a Titan; in the first case, your movement is very important: double jump, wall running, sliding... Mastering the movement is a really ambitious and difficult endeavor, but even with the basics moving is satisfying.
Overall, the guns are fun to use and pretty well designed, even if I find a few of them kind of lacking.
Meanwhile, as a Titan, the gameplay becomes "heavier"; movement is still important, but the game does a great job at making you feel incredibly powerful in a different way. The different Titan loadouts feel fairly balanced and enjoyable.

The campaign, while quite short (around 6 hours), has left quite an impression on me; the story is basic, but even still, it manages to make the characters (even if some appear just briefly) likeable, and the ending is fantastic. But the best thing of the campaign is definitely the level design: EVERY SINGLE level is exceptional and feels unique in its own way.

Getting into the multiplayer today is very difficult, unfortunatly the remaining playerbase is very small, and sometimes even finding matches can take a long time: most gamemodes are pretty much impossible to play; but I still had some fun while playing.

Exemplary video game.
Looks great, plays great, runs great. Awesome, if short, campaign and fun multiplayer that's still alive, although matchmaking can take a minute. You don't really get destroyed by movement gods, not too often anyway, but some familiarity with fast arcade shooters is strongly recommended.
Also, the first game where I've enjoyed a burst fire gun in multiplayer.

I'll forever sing the praises of this game. Everything from the sound design, movement, and gunplay has insane attention to detail and continues to rival that of newer shooters. It was made by people who left Activision to make a better game than COD, and it feels that way. Its core gameplay is unique and well-made; its campaign is a blast (though short); and everything is snappy, responsive, and satisfying. It's a shame the player base and devs have abandoned it for Apex. I wish they'd make a third.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that finding multiplayer matches can take time due to a small player count.

citations.review_text:
So let me preface this review with a clarification: these hours at the time of review are my PC hours on this game. I have been playing the online attrition in this game since day 1, and have played on PS4, XBOX One, and returned to PC, playing a couple matches off and on. I was here in the golden days of initial launch to the DDOS attacks in 2021 (you can google it, don't feel like opening that can of worms here) and hopping from server to server during that whole s**t-show just trying to find games after work. 

     So, getting that out of the way, do I recommend the game still? Yes, it has it's flaws, mainly latency. It is not constant, but when you see another player that looks like they are using instant transmission that appears right in front of you with a fist in your mouth, it's a bit obnoxious and it happens from time to time, but you finish the match and move on. Its definitely not like its prime in those first 5 years, but there is a community that bounced back still keeping this game alive. You can find games (it may take a bit of time to queue initially but once you're in the rotation, you will get games pretty consistently) And when you get into your groove, your controls are dialed in, and you're just moving, you can feel some of that magic still shining through.

   Movement is awesome, customization to how you want to play is great, maps are pretty good, all the bones are still there and they are good bones for a great experience. A good, honest, not very toxic online experience. I am heavily biased to attrition, but there are plenty of other modes, and even co-op in Frontier Defense. We may never get Titanfall 3, but even if we do it's still a good time to get into a good online shooter experience.

Oh right, obviously the campaign is great. but you can see other reviews and articles about that.

Originally played Titanfall 2 on Xbox One when it first came out and I absolutely loved the game because of the gameplay, the designs (especially since I love most things Sci-fi), the soundtrack, the voice acting, and the story, its genuinely one of my all times favorite games. 

I recently played it again here on Steam for fun and inadvertently got most of the achievements on my first campaign run on Steam which led me to get the rest of the achievements I needed just for fun and since I started playing, I have completely fell back in love with this game, it did take me awhile to find some matches due to the low player count but I still had an absolute blast.

I do wish there was a Titanfall 3 and I do have hope that it will happen one day but until then I'll enjoy this game and standby for titanfall.

Edit: Ok I feel like I should give a general progression pipeline for new players, cuz a few of my friends got into the game recently and started with a rough experience.

Never go straight into Multiplayer, especially PvP modes. You WILL be lost, confused, and out-gunned by more experienced players. No amount of gun-skill and aim will save you, but what will save you is information and knowledge, and the campaign is the perfect place for you to try out new stuff and figure stuff out.

Start by playing the campaign and aim to finish the story at least once, as this will provide you with the basic knowledge of player movement and Titan class mechanics. 

The next step after playing the campaign is the PvE mode called Frontier Defense. It is definitely less intense than PvP, but it will let you try out all of the different weapons, Pilot kits and Titan loadouts. In campaign, you only get cloak, and BT is a gigachad of a titan with a playstyle very different from multiplayer titans. This mode offers a structure that lets new players learn the pros and cons of different playstyles in a relatively safe environment.

The PvE mode offers 4 difficulties: Easy, Regular, Hard and Master. Technically theres Insane but we're not going that far. 

-> Easy difficulty is easy, best for learning how to play as a Pilot outside of your Titan. Stick the Assault Chip on your Titan and put them on Guard mode near chokepoints or the Harvester, then run off and do stuff.

--> Regular difficulty is best for figuring out how to play as a Titan and their respective loadouts. Switch your Titan kits around and try them out. 

---> Hard is hard, you'll need a good grasp of both Pilot and Titan combat techniques to win the game as you'll need to know how to fight Titans as a Pilot when your Titan gets destroyed and you eject. It's also the ideal difficulty to push your Titan and Pilot to their limits to see what they can do under extreme si…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that new players will struggle and get out-gunned in PvP multiplayer modes due to the small, highly dedicated, and experienced player base.

citations.review_text:
One of the best FPS games ever created. Great storyline, great level design, great gameplay, great world design, and one of the greatest FPS PvP experiences ever made. I love this game. I wish Apex was never born so this game could have had a chance to survive, but it didn't happen.

Okay, I'm going to stop praising it here because I'm here to talk about the current state of the game. If you're here just to play the single-player, great, do it. It's definitely worth it. But if you also want to try out PvP, here are some warnings.

First, old players will beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of you, and there are only about 1,000–2,000 players a day, so you'll probably run into the same people over and over again. I will say half of the players in this game are friendly, but the other half are super toxic. Since this game is dead, you can pretty much say whatever you want in chat, and no one cares. You're not going to get banned for anything. That also means hackers won't get banned either, and there are a lot of them. Some are really good at hiding it by saying they're just using a controller.

Yes, since I mentioned controllers, I'll tell you how broken they are. Your crosshair will just straight up stick to the enemy, and some players are so good at abusing it that they seem like hackers. (I am a controller player myself. I feel guilty using it, and I mean it.) Well, since it's a 10-year-old game, there are a lot of bugs, and the game is unbalanced. You kind of just have to deal with it.

In the end, I love this game. I truly love this game's story mode and PvP. I really hope Titanfall 3 could happen, but I doubt it. So, for any players who are still playing this game and for newbies who are about to play it, I hope you have a good time.

Good luck, Pilot.
